VANCOUVER, British Columbia–(BUSINESS WIRE)–


**Pan American Silver Corp.** (NYSE: PAAS) (TSX: PAAS) the “Company”) reports exploration results from the vein deposits at its La Colorada mine in Zacatecas, Mexico. The results include the discovery of the high-grade Elena, Denisse and Catalina veins; expansion and infill drilling across several known vein structures; and exploration of the La Chona Breccia orebody.


“These results further demonstrate the extensive scale and continuation of the mineralized system at La Colorada, highlighting the potential to expand mineral inventories and production from existing mine infrastructure while developing the skarn,” said Christopher Emerson, Senior Vice President, Exploration and Geology. “We are particularly encouraged by the discovery of the Elena vein, where drilling and underground development along this vein is exposing exceptionally high-grade silver, gold and base metal mineralization in a vein that remains open to the east and at depth.”


**EXPLORATION HIGHLIGHTS**


**Newly discovered Elena vein**


Elena is a significant new high-grade vein discovery located within the mineralized structural corridor between the NC2 and San Geronimo veins. Initially identified from underground exploration development, follow-up drilling and development have traced the structure for approximately 300 metres along strike and 300 metres vertically. The vein remains a priority for further expansion and infill drilling.


Selected drill results include:


- U-36-26: with **3.39 m grading 760 g/t Ag** , 0.56 g/t Au, 2.14% Pb, 4.16% Zn
- U-44-26: with **1.28 m grading 1,763 g/t Ag** , 0.55 g/t Au, 2.88% Pb, 6.28% Zn
- U-89-26: with **1.06 m grading 1,732 g/t Ag** , 0.34 g/t Au, 11.07% Pb, 20.15% Zn
- U-98-26: with **0.67 m grading 2,177 g/t Ag** , 0.52 g/t Au, 2.17% Pb, 3.16% Zn


**Elena underground development**


Underground development is providing direct exposure to the Elena vein and establishing infrastructure for continued exploration and eventual exploitation of the southern vein system. Initial development and channel sampling along the Elena vein on the 588 level has delineated the mineralized structure averaging **1.07 metres in true width, grading a length-weighted average of 845 g/t Ag, 0.70 g/t Au, 3.96% Pb and 8.61% Zn, over 144 metres of developed strike length** . Subsequent development and channel sampling on the 448 level of nearly **99 metres along strike has exposed an average of** **0.90 metres in true width with a length-weighted average of 1,246 g/t Ag, 6.78 g/t Au, 2.06% Pb and 3.47% Zn** . Underground development continues to progress along strike on the 588 and 448 levels and follow-up drilling is underway with the intention of expanding this exceptionally high-grade mineralization.


**Eastern extensions**


Exploration and infill drilling continues to extend mineralization along the Mariana, NC2, and Estela East veins and appear to support additional mineral resource conversion. The broader vein system along this corridor remains open to the east and at depth.


Selected drill results include:


- S-35-26: with **6.60 m grading 563 g/t Ag** , 0.14 g/t Au, 0.26% Pb, 0.66% Zn (NC2 East)
- U-129-26: with **3.18 m grading 500 g/t Ag** , 0.34 g/t Au, 3.89% Pb, 13.11% Zn (NC2 East)
- U-52-26: with **1.76 m grading 1,597 g/t Ag** , 0.19 g/t Au, 4.25% Pb, 2.63% Zn (NC2 East)
- U-57-26: with **5.46 m grading 373 g/t Ag** , 0.22 g/t Au, 2.02% Pb, 5.68% Zn (NC2 East)
- U-20-26: with **4.46 m grading 598 g/t Ag** , 0.41 g/t Au, 4.26% Pb, 6.20% Zn (Mariana)
- S-48-26: with **2.47 m grading 941 g/t Ag** , 0.06 g/t Au, 0.40% Pb, 0.76% Zn (Denisse)
- S-196-25: with **0.48 m grading 2,149 g/t Ag** , 0.10 g/t Au, 1.62% Pb, 5.04% Zn (Denisse)
- U-42-26: with **7.07 m grading 904 g/t Ag** , 0.70 g/t Au, 3.37% Pb, 4.44% Zn (Estela)
- U-107-26: with **0.93 m grading 1,356 g/t Ag** , 0.11 g/t Au, 0.57% Pb, 10.21% Zn (Estela)
- U-25-26: with **0.32 m grading 2,028 g/t Ag** , 1.60 g/t Au, 12.08% Pb, 17.71% Zn (Estela)
- U-98-26: with **0.77 m grading 2,649 g/t Ag** , 6.39 g/t Au, 0.63% Pb, 0.99% Zn (Catalina)
- U-28-26: with **0.93 m grading 2,430 g/t Ag** , 0.22 g/t Au, 0.19% Pb, 0.45% Zn (Catalina)
- U-105-26: with **0.90 m** **grading 575 g/t Ag** , 0.64 g/t Au, 19.29% Pb, 9.25% Zn (Catalina)


**Filomena and secondary structures**


The Filomena vein and associated secondary structures continue to return high-grade results over a mineralized footprint of approximately **500 metres along strike and 500 metres vertically** , with average estimated true widths of 2.5 metres. The vein and secondary structures remain open to the east and vertically.


Selected drill results include:


- S-09-26: with **3.01 m grading 517 g/t Ag** , 0.71 g/t Au, 10.62% Pb, 17.63% Zn
- S-17-26: with **2.12 m grading 1,373 g/t Ag** , **** 5.23 g/t Au, 3.53% Pb, 5.09% Zn
- S-31-26: with **7.95 m grading 112 g/t Ag** , 0.42 g/t Au, 4.63% Pb, 8.57% Zn
- S-99-26: with **12.21 m grading 67 g/t Ag** , 0.23 g/t Au, 2.71% Pb, 6.60% Zn
- U-116-26: with **2.60 m grading at 570 g/t Ag** , **** 1.23 g/t Au, 4.57% Pb, 8.88% Zn
- U-126-26: with **3.03 m grading 354 g/t Ag** , 0.78 g/t Au, 6.84% Pb, 7.81% Zn


**La Chona Breccia**


La Chona Breccia is a mineralized breccia pipe adjacent to the Filomena vein that has the potential to contribute to future mineral resource growth. Drilling has outlined mineralization over more than **200 metres vertically and 60 metres along strike** , with an average estimated true width exceeding 40 metres. The La Chona Breccia, which remains open for expansion, currently hosts an estimated 567 thousand tonnes of Probable Mineral Reserves grading 136 g/t Ag, 0.10 g/t Au, 0.30% Pb and 1.54% Zn and Inferred Mineral Resources of 446 thousand tonnes grading 144 g/t Ag, 0.10 g/t Au, 0.33% Pb and 1.23% Zn, all of which were included in the Mineral Reserves and Mineral Resources reported for the La Colorada property as at June 30, 2026 (see the news release dated September 16, 2026).


La Chona Breccia differs from the traditional vein-hosted mineralization and skarn mineralization at La Colorada. While grades are lower than those typically encountered in the vein systems, the substantial width and continuity of the breccia body may provide an opportunity for a lower-cost bulk mining method accessible from the vein mine development. Preliminary metallurgical testing has shown recoveries comparable to those achieved in the current vein mining operation.


Selected in-fill drill results include:


- S-103-26: with **53.57 m grading 107 g/t Ag** , 0.08 g/t Au, 0.25% Pb, 1.55% Zn
- S-190-25: with **42.28 m grading 108 g/t Ag** , 0.11 g/t Au, 0.20% Pb, 2.10% Zn
- S-197-25: with **67.20 m grading 127 g/t Ag** , 0.09 g/t Au, 0.34% Pb, 1.82% Zn
- S-67-26: with **89.94 m grading 74 g/t Ag** , 0.05 g/t Au, 0.22% Pb, 1.40% Zn


The exploration results reported in this news release comprise approximately 51,160 metres in 121 drill holes, targeting the veins, and were completed between March 2026 and September 2026. All drill intercepts are reported as estimated true widths in metres (“m”).


Please refer to the “La Colorada Drill Result Highlights” table in this news release for additional details. The full table of drill results, collars, plans and long sections for this period is available at[https://panamericansilver.com/operations/silver-segment/la-colorada/](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fpanamericansilver.com%2Foperations%2Fsilver-segment%2Fla-colorada%2F&esheet=54643025&newsitemid=20261117573295&lan=en-US&anchor=https%3A%2F%2Fpanamericansilver.com%2Foperations%2Fsilver-segment%2Fla-colorada%2F&index=1&md5=6a46dffcd1dfa6412f2ef5d78507d4be) , together with previously reported drill results for La Colorada.

**General Notes with Respect to Technical Information**


Grades are shown as contained metal before mill recoveries are applied. All samples provided in this news release were assayed by ALS Global, Mexico (“ALS”), SGS Durango (“SGS”) and La Colorada Laboratory. At ALS and SGS, using acid digestion with ICP finish for silver, lead, zinc, and copper. For samples above the detection limits of ICP, they were finalized with absorption spectrometry (“AAS”). For lead and zinc grades greater than 30%, the determination was made by volumetric titration. Samples sent to ALS Global were prepared in Zacatecas and Hermosillo, Mexico laboratories and sent to Vancouver, B.C. Laboratory for assay. Samples sent to SGS were prepared and assayed in Durango. At La Colorada Laboratory, gold and silver were assayed by fire assay (20g) and gravimetric finish; for lead, copper, and zinc, sample is digested by aqua regia and finished by AAS. Pan American implements a quality assurance and quality control (“QAQC”) program including the submission of certified standards, blanks, and duplicate samples to the laboratories. The results of the QAQC samples submitted to ALS Global and La Colorada Laboratory demonstrate acceptable accuracy and precision. The Qualified Persons have verified the data disclosed in this news release and they are of the opinion that the sample preparation, analytical, and security procedures followed for the samples are sufficient and reliable for the purpose of any future mineral resource and mineral reserve estimates. There were no limitations on the Qualified Persons’ verification process. Pan American is not aware of any drilling, sampling, recovery or other factors that could materially affect the accuracy or reliability of the data reported herein. ALS Global is independent from Pan American and accredited by ISO/IEC 17025:2017. La Colorada Laboratory is the internal laboratory of the La Colorada Mine, operated by the Company and certified by ISO9001:2015 for Quality Management System.

**Cautionary Note to US Investors**


This news release has been prepared in accordance with the requirements of Canadian NI 43-101 and the Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum Definition Standards, which differ from the requirements of U.S. securities laws. NI 43-101 is a rule developed by the Canadian Securities Administrators that establishes standards for all public disclosure an issuer makes of scientific and technical information concerning mineral projects.


Canadian public disclosure standards, including NI 43-101, differ significantly from the requirements of the SEC, and information concerning mineralization, mineral reserve and mineral resource information contained or referred to herein may not be comparable to similar information disclosed by U.S. companies. The requirements of NI 43-101 for identification of “reserves” are not the same as those of the SEC and may not qualify as “reserves” under SEC standards. Under U.S. standards, mineralization may not be classified as a “reserve” unless the determination has been made that the mineralization could be economically and legally produced or extracted at the time the reserve determination is made. U.S. investors should also understand that “inferred mineral resources” have a great amount of uncertainty as to their existence and great uncertainty as to their economic and legal feasibility. Under Canadian securities laws, estimated “inferred mineral resources” may not form the basis of feasibility or pre-feasibility studies except in rare cases.


**About Pan American**


Pan American is a leading producer of silver and gold in the Americas, operating mines in Canada, Mexico, Peru, Brazil, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina. We also own a 44% joint venture interest in the operating Juanicipio mine in Mexico, a 100% interest in the Escobal mine in Guatemala that is currently not operating, and we hold interests in exploration and development projects. We have been operating in the Americas for over three decades, earning an industry-leading reputation for sustainability performance, operational excellence and prudent financial management. We are headquartered in Vancouver, B.C. and our shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange and the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol “PAAS”.
